evidence.claim: Flagged transaction 3514030 ($77.07, in-person, region 444.0) sits within the card's normal spending range: prior median amount $83.94 and prior maximum $845.01 across 358 prior in-region purchases.

Billing region 444.0 is a known region for this card, not new: 11 prior in-person purchases over 10 days since first use on 2016-09-13, with home-region activity (2 txns) alongside other-region activity (7 txns) in the surrounding 48-hour window.

This card is a heavy roamer with 40 distinct billing regions used all-time, so per the region-novelty rule its use of region 444.0 carries no novelty weight even though the region is a small 3% share of activity.

The $77.07 amount on product code W closely matches a recurring price point on this card ($77.01, 7 prior occurrences, gap CV 0.081, median gap 7.0 days), of which 2 fell in region 444.0 with a 7.2-day median gap and gap CV 0.00, consistent with a repeating legitimate purchase.

The card carries four prior confirmed-fraud closed cases (CC-1066, CC-1673, CC-2964, CC-3587), all opened between July and September 2016, none of them tied to region 444.0, which the card first used on 2016-09-13, after the last of those cases opened.

The case-memory calibration score on the flagged transaction is cms_p=0.2245, well below the real-time risk_score of 0.61 and below the 0.30 case-opening threshold, indicating the memory-informed model does not see this transaction as high risk.

The 72-hour card_window shows nine in-person transactions, all product code W with no online activity and no mixed-channel signal, and card_testing_check/under_threshold_burst returned zero small-amount chain members and zero bursts, ruling out card-testing or burst patterns for this episode.

case.summary: Verdict: legitimate, probability 0.10. The transaction (3514030, $77.07, in-person, billing region 444.0 on 2016-12-04) was reviewed as a real-time risk-score alert (score 0.61) but region 444.0 was already known to the card (11 prior visits since 2016-09-13) and the card is a heavy 40-region roamer, so region novelty carried no weight; the amount closely matched a recurring $77.01 price point on this card (history family) and, after a customer_validation request, the customer confirmed recognizing the purchase and travel to that region (customer family), settling the two-family legitimate read. Exposure is $0.00 since nothing remains unconfirmed; no affected transactions or connected cards/profiles were identified, and pattern is none. Prior closed cases on this same card (CC-1066, CC-2964, CC-3587, CC-1673) were all confirmed out-of-region/new-device fraud from July–September, before region 444.0 was ever used, and similar-case retrieval also surfaced a cleared same-region case (CC-5289), so while an analyst could reasonably have read this as a repeat of the card's out_of_region_use fraud history absent the confirmation, the recurring-charge match plus the customer's confirmation tip it to legitimate. Recommended route: auto — CREATE_CASE (a case was opened when evidence was requested), ALLOW_TRANSACTION, and CLOSE_NO_FRAUD per R3; had the customer instead denied the charge, R2 would have required BLOCK_CARD (L1) and CREATE_CASE.
